prompt: Build a command line from raw key events: keyTyped handles printable characters, backspace and enter (with a trimmed, bounded history), and keyPressed recalls the newest command on the Up arrow.
explanation: keyTyped and keyPressed answer different questions: keyTyped reports the character produced, which is the only way to see backspace and enter as '\b' and '\n', while keyPressed reports physical keys such as VK_UP that produce no character at all. Handling both in one KeyAdapter keeps the editing rules together. The bounded history uses the classic trick of appending then removing index 0 when the size exceeds the cap, and every destructive operation is guarded by an emptiness check so no keystroke can throw.
hints: One anonymous KeyAdapter can override both keyTyped and keyPressed -- you do not need two separate listeners.
Character.isISOControl(ch) is true for backspace, enter, tab and friends, so test the two you care about first and ignore the rest.
After adding to the history, drop history.remove(0) whenever history.size() exceeds the maximum, so the oldest entry falls off the front.
